text: HTTPS is the foundation of secure web communication, encrypting data between users and servers to prevent eavesdropping. Authentication ensures only authorized users access sensitive areas, often through passwords or multi-factor verification. Input validation is equally critical: never trust user data. Attackers exploit unverified forms to inject malicious code or SQL commands, leading to data breaches or site defacement. Common vulnerabilities include cross-site scripting (XSS), where scripts run in browsers, and SQL injection, which manipulates databases. Developers must sanitize inputs, use parameterized queries, and keep software updated. A single overlooked flaw can compromise entire systems, so security must be woven into every layer of development, not added as an afterthought.
